extracted.intended_audience: short-story authors, literary editors, critics, and literary historians compiling or evaluating annual 'best of' lists
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and procedural rules used by a literary yearbook to select, rank, and index the most 'distinctive' short stories published in American periodicals in 1917. Includes both literary-quality criteria (voice, characterization, originality, atmosphere) and selection/indexing rules (asterisk system, exclusion of reprints, tie-breaking).

rubrics_metrics.name: Asterisk distinction system (one/two/three asterisks)
rubrics_metrics.description: One, two, and three asterisks are employed to indicate relative distinction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-asterisk stories are of somewhat permanent literary value. Three-asterisk stories entitle a title to a place on the annual "Rolls of Honor." (Lists that tabulate one-, two-, and three-asterisk stories exclude reprints.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-asterisk = permanent literary value
rubrics_metrics.description: "Three-asterisk stories" are of somewhat permanent literary value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-asterisk stories are considered to have more or less permanent literary value and are entitled to the annual "Rolls of Honor."

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of reprints from distinction lists
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of distinctive stories and periodical tallies excludes reprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When counting or assigning asterisks, reprints are not considered; only original publications during the year are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asterisk before author's name indicates non-American author
rubrics_metrics.description: An asterisk before the name of an author indicates that he is not an American.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the index to flag nationality of contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie-breaking by relative rank in other lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Ties in the ranking lists are decided by taking relative rank in other lists into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When two periodicals or entries tie on a given metric, other ranking lists are consulted to break the tie.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magazine/periodical evaluation by counts and percentages of "distinctive" stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodicals are evaluated by number of stories published, number of distinctive stories published, and percentage of distinctive stories published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The yearbook tabulates NO. OF STORIES PUBLISHED, NO. OF DISTINCTIVE STORIES PUBLISHED, and PERCENTAGE OF DISTINCTIVE STORIES PUBLISHED for each periodical to rank them both by percentage and by absolute number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of indexing (which publications and omissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: All short stories published in the following magazines and newspapers during 1917 are indexed; certain issues not procurable were omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Index lists a broad set of periodicals (American Magazine, Atlantic Monthly, Harper's, Scribner's, etc.). The yearbook specifies omissions (e.g., Oct/Nov issues of the Masses not listed because not procurable; Oct. issue of Little Review withdrawn). This procedural scope determines which stories were eligible for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic spiritual message as a criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories with 'authentic spiritual message' are singled out as distinguished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a story described as one of the three stories with the most authentic spiritual message in American fiction produced by the war — spiritual sincerity/authority is treated as a mark of distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convincing character portrait / faithful rendering of personality
rubrics_metrics.description: A convincing character portrait that ranks with the better short stories of recognized authors is a mark of distinction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise is given for faithful rendering of a personality (e.g., 'added a convincing character portrait to American letters...'), and portraits rendered with 'incisive kindliness' or 'artistic sincerity' are valued. By contrast, portraits that create a 'conventional atmosphere' may be criticized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative situation and legendary / folk quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Realization of a fine imaginative situation and presentation of a folk story with significant legendary quality are criteria for distinction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works in the tradition of Hawthorne or the folk-story tradition are praised when they handle the substance of the author's own people, giving free scope to the creative impulse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic voice and originality (avoid mere imitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Capturing an authentic voice without being a mere imitator is an evaluative standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imitation of a master (e.g., 'O. Henry') is criticized as a curse; praise is given when a writer achieves the 'authentic voice' yet remains an original creator and may become a successor rather than an imitator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-specific judgment (verse vs prose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Short stories in verse are judged on the same literary standards and can be preferred if they achieve imaginative fulfilment comparable to prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a short story in verse is called 'the best short story in verse that the year has produced' and is said to 'realize ... greater imaginative fulfilment' than a well-known prose work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fresh treatment of old themes / discovery of new values
rubrics_metrics.description: Treating an old theme freshly and discovering new values (e.g., in contrasting character) marks a story as notable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that find 'new values' in well-worn subjects and 'justify the author's calling' are singled out for praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atmospheric realism and unadorned power
rubrics_metrics.description: Stark or brutal realism that convincingly renders atmosphere, even if it repels some readers, is considered valuable when psychologically convincing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories 'woven out of the simplest elements' and lacking literary sophistication can still be compared favorably to strong works if they have 'entire lack of literary sophistication' yet 'power and convincing quality.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtlety, reticence, and psychological inevitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Reticent handling of tragic circumstance, subtle background rendering, and action that feels inevitable are criteria of high quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories praised as 'reticently handled' with 'subtly rendered' backgrounds that influence character and produce action that is 'inevitable despite its character of surprise' demonstrate this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gift of selection to highlight psychological contrasts
rubrics_metrics.description: A writer's 'gift of selection' — the ability to bring out the most illusive psychological contrasts — is a positive criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection that isolates the most illusive contrasts and creates memorable psychological effects is cited as especially distinctive (used to praise supernatural/psychological stories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pictorial presentation of action and spiritual conflict; sense of human mystery
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting action and spiritual conflict pictorially, with a rich sense of human mystery and appropriate tragic humor or hopeful philosophy, is valued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors whose work 'presents action and spiritual conflict pictorially' and who convey 'a sense of human mystery' akin to established masters are ranked highly.
